scope: Follow-up budget sensitivity after all six P20 outputs hit the 4096 output cap. Same known development state, public inputs, model, instructions, seeds and order; both arms now get 8192 output tokens. Not new independent tasks, not a novel method or end-to-end success comparison.
evaluation: After all six generations: interpret code without environment access; compare every CSV with task-specific analyst-derived public observation union. Include format, program and budget failures. No free retry or target-count hints.
limitations: Both arms receive a common structured observation packet, not the original full conversation. Do not infer a causal effect by comparing against the original P18 output alone.
Interpreter capabilities and prompt overhead differ as the intended output mechanism; record all input and output costs.
The restricted interpreter is not a general Python agent. Unsupported code cannot establish that ordinary CodeAct would fail.
No account operation, model-generated CSV, missing title, target count, hidden evaluation or reserved task is provided as input.
P20 failures and costs are retained separately. This post-hoc budget choice is not a prespecified confirmatory study; no automatic further cap doubling if submissions remain absent.
